it-2008-it-2.approach: Convert the complement probabilities to $P(A)$ and $P(B)$ and apply the addition rule.

steps.title: Find P(A) and P(B)
steps.body: $P(A) = 1 - P(\overline{A}) = 1 - \tfrac13 = \tfrac23$, and likewise $P(B) = \tfrac23$.

steps.title: Addition rule
steps.body: $$P(A\cup B) = P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B) = \tfrac23+\tfrac23-\tfrac12 = \tfrac{8}{12}+\tfrac{8}{12}-\tfrac{6}{12} = \tfrac{10}{12}.$$

$9/12$ would need $P(A\cap B)=7/12$.
$8/12$ is just $P(A)$; it ignores the contribution of $B$.

it-2008-it-3.approach: A 3×3 grid is bipartite (colour by parity of row+column). The extra curved edge joins two corners of the same parity, creating an odd cycle, so exactly 3 colours are needed.

steps.body: Label vertices $(r,c)$ with $r,c\in\{0,1,2\}$. Grid edges join cells whose $r+c$ differ by 1, so colouring by the parity of $r+c$ is proper: 2 colours.

steps.title: The curved edge creates an odd cycle
steps.body: The extra edge joins the top-left $(0,0)$ ($r+c=0$, even) and the bottom-right $(2,2)$ ($r+c=4$, even) — same parity. A grid path between them has length 4, so with the curved edge we get a cycle of length $4+1=5$ (odd). Thus $\chi\ge 3$.

steps.title: Three colours suffice
steps.body: Keep the parity colouring and recolour only $(2,2)$ with a third colour. Its grid neighbours $(1,2)$, $(2,1)$ have the odd colour and $(0,0)$ the even colour, so the colouring stays proper. Hence $\chi = 3$.

it-2008-it-6.approach: Subset construction turns an n-state NFA into a DFA with at most $2^n$ states, and minimisation never increases the count.

steps.title: Upper bound
steps.body: The subset construction gives a DFA whose states are subsets of the $n$ NFA states: at most $2^n$. The minimal DFA $M$ is no larger, so $m \le 2^n$ always.

steps.title: Why the others fail
steps.body:
- $n\le m$ fails: an NFA may be redundant, e.g. a 5-state NFA for $\Sigma^*$ while the minimal DFA has 1 state.
- One accept state fails: the minimal DFA for $\{\varepsilon, a\}$ over $\{a\}$ has 2 accepting states.
- $m = 2^n$ holds only for special worst-case languages.

A redundant NFA can have more states than the minimal DFA.
